title: ¡Hola!
subtitle: Four ways to say hello and goodbye
register: casual (tú), a couple at home, Mexican Spanish
review: Written by Claude in Latin American (Mexican) Spanish. Check the Spanish, the English lines, the notes and the questions.
intro: A phone call from the next room, an honest answer to 'how are you?', a trip to the store that may last until tomorrow, and a goodbye with seven aunts in the way: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for which greeting fits which moment, and for the small words Mexico adds: ¿bueno?, ahorita, al rato.

tr.en: Hello?

lines.note: How Mexicans answer the phone. Nowhere else, and never face to face.

tr.en: Hi, good morning.
Good morning. Who's this?

lines.note: ¿Quién habla?: who is speaking?

tr.en: Emma. Your wife.
Oh, hi, honey. Where are you?

lines.note: Mi amor: the everyday 'honey' between couples.

tr.en: In the kitchen.

lines.text: ¿Y por qué me llamas por teléfono?

tr.en: Then why are you phoning me?

lines.text: Porque te dije «buenos días» tres veces y no contestaste.

tr.en: Because I said good morning three times and you didn't answer.

lines.note: Contestar: to answer.

tr.en: Sorry. I've got my headphones on.

lines.note: Traer: to bring, and in Mexico also to be wearing or carrying.

lines.text: Ya vi. El desayuno estaba listo.

tr.en: So I see. Breakfast was ready.

lines.note: Estaba: was. The past tense is the whole message.

tr.en: Hi! How are you?

lines.text: Mal. Dormí poco, me duele la espalda y no hay café.

tr.en: Bad. I hardly slept, my back hurts and there's no coffee.

lines.note: Me duele…: my … hurts. No hay: there isn't any.

tr.en: Lucas. It was a greeting.

lines.note: Un saludo: a greeting. Saludar: to greet.

tr.en: Oh. Again?

lines.note: Otra vez: once more.

tr.en: Hi, how are you?
Fine, thanks. And you?

lines.note: The answer everyone expects.

tr.en: Very well. See how easy that is?

lines.text: Sí. Pero todavía no hay café.

tr.en: Yes. But there's still no coffee.

lines.note: Todavía: still.

lines.text: Bueno, ya me voy. Ahorita vengo.

tr.en: Right, I'm off. I'll be right back.

lines.note: Ya me voy: I'm leaving now. Ahorita vengo: I'll be right back.

tr.en: Where are you going?

lines.text: A la tienda. No me tardo.

tr.en: To the store. I won't be long.

lines.note: Tardarse: to take a long time.

lines.text: ¿«Ahorita» de cinco minutos o «ahorita» de tres horas?

tr.en: 'Right back' as in five minutes, or as in three hours?

lines.note: Ahorita: right now, soon, or some day. Every Mexican knows the difference by the tone.

tr.en: Right back.
Then see you tomorrow.

lines.note: Nos vemos + when: see you…

tr.en: Don't exaggerate! See you in a bit.

lines.note: Al rato: in a while. To a man: ¡qué exagerado!

lines.text: Cuídate. Y salúdame a tu compadre.

tr.en: Take care. And say hi to your buddy for me.

lines.note: Salúdame a…: say hello to … for me. Compadre: a close friend.

tr.en: How do you know that…? I will.

lines.note: De tu parte is the set reply to salúdame a…: 'on your behalf'.

tr.en: Lucas, let's go now. It's late.

lines.note: Vámonos: let's go. Ya makes it 'now'.

tr.en: Yes. I've already said goodbye.

lines.note: Despedirse: to say goodbye.

tr.en: You said goodbye an hour ago.

lines.note: Hace + a time: … ago.

tr.en: I still have my aunts to go.

lines.note: Me faltan…: I still have … left.

tr.en: How many aunts do you have?

lines.text: Siete. Y todas quieren un abrazo.

tr.en: Seven. And they all want a hug.

lines.note: Un abrazo: a hug. Nobody leaves a Mexican family party without one from everybody.

tr.en: OK. See you later, then.
Where are you going?

lines.text: A dormir en el coche. Buenas noches.

tr.en: To sleep in the car. Good night.

notes: Hello by the clock: buenos días until noon, buenas tardes until dark, buenas noches after dark and at bedtime. Hola works all day.
¿Cómo estás? is a greeting more than a question. The expected answer is bien, gracias, ¿y tú?
¿Bueno? is only for answering the phone, and only in Mexico.
Leaving: ya me voy (I'm leaving), ya vámonos (let's go), ahorita vengo (I'll be right back), no me tardo (I won't be long).
Goodbyes: nos vemos, nos vemos al rato, hasta luego, hasta mañana, cuídate.
Salúdame a tu mamá: say hi to your mom for me. The reply is de tu parte.

questions.q: The phone rings in Mexico. What does Lucas say when he answers?
questions.why: ¿Bueno? is the Mexican 'hello?' on the phone.

questions.q: « ¿Cómo estás? » What answer does Emma expect?
questions.why: It is a greeting. The usual reply is bien, gracias, ¿y tú?

questions.q: Lucas says he will be right back. What does he say?
questions.why: Ahorita vengo = I'll be right back. How soon is another matter.

questions.q: « Salúdame a tu compadre. » What is the set reply?
questions.why: De tu parte: I will say hello on your behalf.

questions.q: Why can't Lucas leave the party?
options: He has lost the car keys.
He still has seven aunts to say goodbye to.
questions.why: Me faltan mis tías: I still have my aunts to go. They all want a hug.
